biography: Joel 'Flash' Heinrich hails from the sun-baked landscapes of rural South Australia. Growing up on his family's sheep farm, Joel's first taste of speed came not from asphalt, but from tearing across the paddocks on a beat-up quad bike. He entered his first local karting race at 16, funded by shearing sheep and fueled by raw ambition. His aggressive style immediately caught attention. A defining moment came at the Australian Karting Championships when, despite starting last after a mechanical failure, he clawed his way to second place, cementing his reputation as a fearless overtaker. Now in his mid-thirties, Joel is considered to be at the peak of his abilities and is a stalwart of the Team Redlight squad, known for his unwavering commitment and occasional controversial on-track maneuvers. He is chasing his first major championship, determined to prove he's more than just a flashy showman.
drivingStyle: Heinrich's driving style is characterized by audacious late-braking maneuvers and an unwavering commitment to attacking corners. He thrives under pressure, often pushing his car to the absolute limit. Tire management isn't his forte; he prefers an all-out assault, sacrificing long-term pace for immediate gains. Some consider him reckless, but his ability to pull off seemingly impossible overtakes is undeniable. He has a knack for exploiting even the smallest gaps, often leaving rivals shaking their heads in disbelief.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision at the Adelaide 500, where Heinrich's aggressive move forced Silva into retirement.
A clash of personalities and driving styles. Dubois, known for her calculated precision, clashes with Heinrich's more impulsive approach, leading to frequent on-track battles and off-track barbs.

famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser. You race to win, or you don't race at all.
careerHighlight: Winning the Bathurst 1000 in 2020 with a daring last-lap overtake, solidifying his place in Australian motorsport history.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2022 Gold Coast 600, costing him a crucial championship point.
